feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
The discussion raises important questions about the necessity and functionality of the SIGHASH_SCRIPTMASK flag in Bitcoin's transaction signing process. The primary concern is whether this flag serves any practical purpose, as its intended effect—removing a mask during signing—could arguably be performed by default without requiring explicit instruction from the flag. This perspective highlights a potential redundancy in the design, suggesting that always applying mask removal might streamline the process and reduce complexity.
Attention is also given to how scriptmask operates within the context of Taproot, the recent Bitcoin upgrade that allows for greater privacy and flexibility by enabling scripts to remain hidden unless needed. In this environment, the relevance of scriptmask becomes even more questionable, since alternative scripts are concealed and can be constructed with much broader capabilities. If arbitrary scripts can be signed or used, the original rationale for the scriptmask seems diminished.
These points collectively challenge some established assumptions about transaction signing mechanics and flag utility in evolving Bitcoin protocols. The inquiry invites further exploration and clarification from experts, especially regarding potential security implications or overlooked use cases where explicit mask-removal flags might still be valuable despite apparent redundancy. Additional insights and continuing conversation can be tracked on the [bitcoin-dev mailing list](https://lists.linuxfoundation.org/mailman/listinfo/bitcoin-dev).
